option_relations.rationale: Metastatic melanoma is a type of cancer that spreads to the liver, but it is not hepatocellular carcinoma. The S100-negative variant refers to a specific characteristic of melanoma cells, which is not directly related to hepatocellular carcinoma.
Hepatic angiomyolipoma is a benign tumor of the liver composed of blood vessels, smooth muscle, and fat. It is distinct from hepatocellular carcinoma, which is a malignant tumor of hepatocytes.
Angiosarcoma is a rare, aggressive malignant tumor of endothelial cells that can occur in the liver. It is a different type of cancer than hepatocellular carcinoma.
Perivascular endothelial carcinoma (PEComa) of the liver is a rare mesenchymal tumor. It is not hepatocellular carcinoma.
